source_text: Ἐπείπερ, ὡς ἄρχει ὁ Θεὸς ἁπάσης τῆς γῆς καὶ τῶν ἐν αὐτῇ πάντων, οὕτω καὶ τὸν ἄνθρωπον δεύτερον ἄρχοντα πάσης τῆς γῆς καὶ τῶν ἐν αὐτῇ κατέστησε, τοῦτο εἶναι τὸ κατ' εἰκόνα Θεοῦ καὶ καθ' ὁμοίωσιν γενέσθαι τὸν ἄνθρωπόν φημι. 87 Καὶ εἶπεν ὁ Θεός· ποιήσωμεν ἄνθρωπον κατ' εἰκόνα ἡμετέραν καὶ καθ' ὁμοίωσιν. Ἀλλὰ πρὸς τίνα ἔφη· ζητήσωμεν, φιλόσοφε;
thought_title: The second ruler and the plural 'let us make'
orientation: Eustathius is answering the philosopher, having just identified humanity's ruling over the earth as the chief point of being made in God's image; he now states this as his own conclusion and turns to the plural 'let us make' in Genesis 1:26.
pass_a_gloss: Since, as God rules all the earth and all things in it, so also he appointed the human being as a second ruler of all the earth and of the things in it, I say that this is the being made in God's image and in God's likeness for the human being. And God said: let us make a human being according to our image and according to likeness. But to whom did he say: let us seek, philosopher?

choices.why: Keeps the adjective 'second' explicit, matching Eustathius's point that humanity rules under God as a subordinate ruler.
Renders the causative force of καθίστημι: God set the human being in the position of ruler.

choices.term: τοῦτο εἶναι τὸ κατ' εἰκόνα Θεοῦ καὶ καθ' ὁμοίωσιν γενέσθαι τὸν ἄνθρωπόν φημι
choices.english: I say that this is the being made in God's image and in God's likeness for the human being
choices.why: Preserves the word order and the infinitive construction, keeping 'I say' at the end as in the Greek.
rejected: I say that this is what it means for the human being to be made in God's image and likeness

choices.term: ποιήσωμεν ἄνθρωπον κατ' εἰκόνα ἡμετέραν καὶ καθ' ὁμοίωσιν
choices.english: let us make a human being according to our image and according to likeness
choices.why: Uses the glossary rendering 'let us make' and keeps the possessive 'our' on image while leaving likeness unqualified, as in the source.
rejected: let us make man in our image and likeness

choices.why: Renders the hortatory subjunctive literally; Eustathius shifts from 'let us make' to 'let us seek' as he poses the question.

bible_refs.note: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ Θεός· ποιήσωμεν ἄνθρωπον κατ' εἰκόνα ἡμετέραν καὶ καθ' ὁμοίωσιν

pass_b_english: Since God rules all the earth and everything in it, and in the same way appointed the human being as a second ruler over all the earth and everything in it, I say that this is what it means for the human being to be made in God's image and in God's likeness. And God said, “Let us make a human being in our image and in our likeness” (Genesis 1:26). But to whom did he say it? Let us investigate, philosopher.

problems.source_quote: ποιήσωμεν ἄνθρωπον κατ' εἰκόνα ἡμετέραν καὶ καθ' ὁμοίωσιν. Ἀλλὰ πρὸς τίνα ἔφη· ζητήσωμεν, φιλόσοφε;
problems.why: The quotation "Let us seek" mistranslates ζητήσωμεν; Eustathius asks "let us seek" (investigate), not quoting Genesis.
problems.fix: But to whom did he say it? Let us investigate, philosopher.

edits.old: But to whom did he say, “Let us seek,” philosopher?
edits.new: But to whom did he say it? Let us investigate, philosopher.

last_rejected.why: Glossary requires 'in God's likeness' not 'in our likeness' for this term.
last_rejected.fix: in God's image and in God's likeness
last_rejected.ruling: Source has καθ' ὁμοίωσιν without pronoun; 'our' reflects ἡμετέραν from the Genesis quote, not a glossary error.
